2607.18884.title: Public perceptions of AI-driven decision-making in healthcare: A structural equation modeling approach
2607.18884.paper_summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare to support diagnostics, decision-making, and administrative processes. However, the successful implementation of AI depends not only on technical performance but also on public perceptions of its helpfulness, riskiness, and fairness. This study examines public perceptions of automated decision-making (ADM) in healthcare. Data were drawn from the first wave of an ongoing longitudinal survey panel. The final sample consisted of 3,915 respondents and was analyzed with structural equation modeling. Perceptions of ADM in healthcare as helpful, risky, and fair were treated as the dependent variables. AI literacy, familiarity with different forms of AI, confidence in clinicians' ability to distinguish AI- from human-generated content, use of conversational agents for health information, and use of traditional digital health information sources were included as exogenous. Greater familiarity with different forms of AI, higher confidence in the clinician's ability to recognize AI-generated content, and use of conversational agents for health information were associated with greater perceived helpfulness. Use of conversational agents was associated with lower perceived risk, whereas greater familiarity with AI and greater reliance on traditional health information sources were associated with higher perceived risk. Perceptions of ADM as fair were most strongly predicted by confidence in the clinician's ability, with additional small positive associations with AI familiarity, AI literacy, and use of conversational agents. Public perceptions of ADM in healthcare are shaped by technological familiarity, use of conversational agents, and confidence in human oversight. Overall, ADM's perceived helpfulness and fairness are driven more by trust in healthcare professionals than by trust in the technology itself.
2607.18884.paper_summary_zh: 人工智慧（AI）越來越多地融入醫療保健，以支持診斷、決策和行政流程。<lb/>然而，AI的成功實施不僅取決於技術性能，還取決於公眾對其有用性、風險性和公平性的看法。<lb/>本研究探討了公眾對醫療保健中自動化決策（ADM）的看法。<lb/>數據來自一項正在進行的縱向調查面板的第一波。<lb/>最終樣本包含3,915名受訪者，並使用結構方程模型進行分析。<lb/>對醫療保健中ADM的看法被視為有用的、風險的和公平的，並作為依賴變數。<lb/>AI素養、對不同形式AI的熟悉程度、對臨床醫生區分AI生成內容與人類生成內容能力的信心、使用對話代理獲取健康信息的情況以及使用傳統數字健康信息來源的情況被納入為外生變數。<lb/>對不同形式AI的更高熟悉度、對臨床醫生識別AI生成內容能力的更高信心以及使用對話代理獲取健康信息與更高的有用性感知相關聯。<lb/>使用對話代理與較低的風險感知相關，而對AI的更高熟悉度和對傳統健康信息來源的更大依賴則與較高的風險感知相關。<lb/>對ADM的公平性感知最強烈地受到對臨床醫生能力的信心的預測，並與AI熟悉度、AI素養和使用對話代理有額外的小幅正相關。<lb/>公眾對醫療保健中ADM的看法受到技術熟悉度、使用對話代理和對人類監督的信心的影響。<lb/>總體而言，ADM的有用性感知和公平性更多地受到對醫療專業人員的信任驅動，而非對技術本身的信任。
